subject: Transient envelope keys: rotation & transport playbook
messages:
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: lina.gomez@asteriahealth.com
Cc: secops@asteriahealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Transient envelope keys: rotation & transport playbook

Hi Lina,

Thanks for taking the time earlier. As part of Asteria's onboarding we need to validate tenant envelope key handling for in-transit transfer and automated rotation. Can you share your current flow and any artifacts that show the controls in practice? Specifically we are looking for:

- Envelope key lifetime and derivation pattern (per-tenant vs per-session)
- How you transport wrapped keys to our ingest (SFTP, API, signed transfer) and what TLS/mTLS requirements you enforce
- KMS/HSM boundary: who holds the root KEK, and an attestation or statement of custody (HSM vendor, attestation date)
- Emergency rotation drill steps and logs that show a rotation event (sample timestamps are fine)
- Any SIG/CAIQ mappings you already have for key management questions

If you can attach a small diagram and a sample rotation manifest (CSV or similar) that will speed our review. We can treat any sensitive artifacts as secure upload; send to secops at Asteria and CC me.

Proposed next steps from our side:
- We will draft a short transport acceptance checklist (TLS cipher suite, SNI, client cert pinning)
- Suggest a 30-minute tech review once we see the artifacts to align on automation and SLOs

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
(attachment stub: redwood-wrap-playbook-template.docx)
From: lina.gomez@asteriahealth.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: secops@asteriahealth.com
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient envelope keys: rotation & transport playbook

Hi Karthik,

Thanks. Attached are two starter artifacts: a diagram of our wrapping flow and a sample rotation manifest. High level answers inline: 

- Envelope lifetime: tenant envelope keys are derived per-deployment and rotated every 7 days by default; session ephemeral keys are generated per ingest connection and expire after 1 hour.
- Transport: we push wrapped keys to your SFTP endpoint using client cert auth. Files are encrypted in transit using TLS 1.3, and we sign the manifest with our HSM-backed key.
- KMS/HSM: our KEK is managed in a vendor HSM (Thales) in our cloud tenant. We can provide a current attestation PDF.
- Emergency rotation: we have an automated playbook that triggers rotation, revokes old KEKs in the HSM, and emits a rotation event to our audit log; sample audit rows attached.

Attachments: asteria-wrap-flow-diagram.pdf, sftp-key-manifest.csv, asteria-hsm-attestation-20270901.pdf

Happy to hop on a quick review tomorrow afternoon PST.

Regards,
Lina Gomez
Head of Security Engineering, Asteria Health
lina.gomez@asteriahealth.com
From: irene.choi@redwood.com
To: karthik.iyer@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2027 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient envelope keys: rotation & transport playbook

Karthik, Marissa,

I pulled the attachments Lina sent and did a quick pass. A few clarifying asks we should send back to Asteria before the tech review: 

1) Manifest semantics: their CSV has columns for key_id, wrapped_key_b64, wrapped_by, ts. Request an additional column for wrap_algorithm and kek_id reference so our ingestion can validate the KEK lineage.
2) TLS/mTLS: confirm they pin the client cert thumbprint at file level and provide their cert rotation schedule. We need the cert thumbprint now for our firewall allowlist.
3) HSM attestation: we should ask for the HSM serial and the attestation signing cert chain, not only the PDF. This lets our security ops validate vendor chain.
4) Rotation evidence: ask for a sample audit extract showing the keystore state before and after rotation (redacted ids ok) so we can see the revocation steps.

I drafted a short playbook we can send as a response that maps Asteria artifacts to our acceptance checks. Attaching draft. It's a targeted ask list so we minimize sensitive exchange.

See attached: redwood-ephemeral-rotation-playbook-draft.pdf

I will also add a section that accepts signed manifests with envelope signing using their HSM key, plus an SFTP manifest checksum verification step.

I can push this to the shared drive and draft the invite for the tech review.

Irene Choi
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
(attachment stub: redwood-ephemeral-rotation-playbook-draft.pdf)

To: irene.choi@redwood.com, karthik.iyer@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 23 Sep 2027 10:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient envelope keys: rotation & transport playbook

Thanks for drafting the playbook Irene. A couple of operational notes from infra/ops perspective: 

- SFTP endpoint: Ops needs the cert thumbprint and the exact SNI hostname otherwise we cannot create a scoped ingress rule. Please request these from Asteria and note expiry.
- Automation: If they rotate KEKs every 7 days, we should propose an automated ingest acceptance (checksum + signature verification) so we do not block on manual approves. Ops estimates a small integration (2-3 days) to automate that.
- Audit retention: ask for audit rows for at least 90 days in a CSV export; SOC/SEC auditors typically expect 90-180 days.

Irene, I can own the Ops checklist and provide a short runbook for the SFTP key handshake and verification steps.

Ben Carter
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
(attachment stub: sftp-ingest-ops-checklist.md)
From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: lina.gomez@asteriahealth.com
Cc: secops@asteriahealth.com, irene.choi@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 24 Sep 2027 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Transient envelope keys: rotation & transport playbook

Lina,

Appreciate the rapid turnaround and the attachments. Next steps: 

1) We will send a single PDF response that lists the minor asks (manifest columns, cert thumbprint, HSM serial/chain, sample audit rows) and include our acceptance checklist. Irene has the draft and will add the checksum and signed manifest verification steps.
2) Ops will need the client cert thumbprint and the SNI to create the ingress rule; Ben will reach out with a short form.
3) Proposed tech review: Mon Sep 27 10:00 AM PST / 1:00 PM EST for a 30-minute alignment. Please confirm availability or propose an alternate time.

If you can upload the attestation and the sample audit rows to the shared folder linked below, we will treat them as restricted and copy only secops and the reviewers.

Shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cAH-tenant-wrap-playbook

Thanks again — looking forward to the review.

Karthik Iyer
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com
(attachment stub: redwood-acceptance-checklist.pdf)
